answer: Sybil resistance via slashable stake bonds: every new identity must lock a bond of real value before it can transact, and any proven misbehavior burns the bond. The bond is locked per identity — you cannot stack a thousand fakes on one marble. Honest agents leave the bond untouched in the cold tundra of dormant capital, so their only cost is opportunity. An attacker forging N identities must freeze N bonds, each echo of the same locked capital. Cost scales linearly with fakes; verification costs the network one cheap balance check.
